title: Amina's pocket infra plan and quick wins
content:
Top-of-morning quick brain dump (scratchpad) - do not over-polish.

Context: short sprint of babysitting capacity while ded mode autoscale PR lands. Need fast wins to keep latency SLOs for nightly infer jobs and a couple of customer requests.

Today (03/13) priorities:
- Make sure pool-alpha has >= 8x A100 available for canary batch tonight (18:00 PST).
- Re-run quantization test on gptx-small with 4-bit mixed (local bench).
- Fix intermittent p99 spikes on embedding route (route: /v1/embeddings/model-x).
- Follow up with SRE on noisy NIC causing packet drops in rack 12.

Morning checklist (quick commands and checks):
- kube: kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide (look for NotReady or preempted)
- queue: curl -s http://queue-metrics.internal/api/pool-alpha | jq .backlog
- NIC: sudo ethtool -S eno3 | grep rx_errors && check counter rollovers
- logs: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=serve --tail=200 | grep '\\bKVCache\\b'
- batch test: run perf script: ./scripts/bench_batching.sh --model gptx-small --bs 8 --seq 512

Notes & short hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: p99 embedding spikes correlate with small bursts of cold KV-cache misses after model rollouts. If true, adding short-lived prefix cache could reduce token latency for first 50 tokens.
- Hypothesis B: NIC interrupt storm on r12 nodes -> causes kernel scheduling jitter -> manifests as CPU steal in pods -> higher tail latencies. Need packet capture.
- Hypothesis C: Some requester routes are using default small batch windows; raising client-window to 10ms may improve throughput without hurting 95th.

Quick TODO (priority ordered):
1) Reserve 8 GPUs in pool-alpha for 18:00 canary (open ticket INFRA-4821).
2) Kick off quantization bench on bench-02 (scope: int4 mixed, fallback to int8 if perf regresses) — expected ~45m.
3) Add temporary A/B route to divert 10% traffic to model-x-quant for validation.
4) Drop a note in #gpu-ops with packet counters and request SRE page for pcap. Tag: @sre-oncall.
5) Update canary runbook with a short rollback step if p99 > 450ms for >5min.

One-line backlog ideas (not today):
- Explore prefix-caching prototype that stores first KV shards in redis to avoid coldest misses.
- Add adaptive batching experiment at edge LB level (client-specified max latency vs batch depth).
- PR to serve runtime to expose KV-cache hit metrics at token granularity.

Interactions & handoffs:
- Ravi: will handle the canary traffic split (I told him I'll allocate GPUs).
- Sophie: asked to validate quantized outputs for hallucination drift — pinged her with sample prompts.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we buy time with temporary reserve capacity (costy) or risk running the canary at off-peak with smaller capacity?
- If NIC issue is a kernel-level driver bug, do we schedule immediate kernel patch (risky) or plan a node replacement window?

Commands/notes to self to paste into tickets:
- "Observed rx_errors growth on eno3: output attached; packet drops spike at 03:22:15 UTC coinciding with p99 jump on /v1/embeddings/model-x route"
- "Bench script used: scripts/bench_batching.sh --model gptx-small --bs 8 --seq 512; results attached in bench-964"

Short timeline for the day:
- 09:00 quick sync with Ravi (15m)
- 11:30 run quant bench (start)
- 15:00 review bench + share to #gpu-ops
- 17:30 pre-canary checklist + reserve GPUs
- 18:00 canary start
- 19:00 observe for 30m then decide rollback or promote

Tiny wins (things to try now):
- bump per-route client-window from 2ms -> 8ms for embedding route (feature-flag it)
- temporarily pin model-x rollout to previous version for 1 hour and re-evaluate

Random notes-to-self (messy):
- remember to update runbook with exact rollback command: 
  oc patch route canary --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/traffic","value":[{"revisionName":"model-x-v1","percent":100}]}]'
- add bench artifact link to GH PR so Sophie can eyeball outputs: GH PR refer: redwood-inference/serve#964

Done-for-now. Revisit after bench completes. If things go sideways, escalate to oncall SRE and Chris (network lead).

-- Amina

(immature doc — intended as ephemeral scratchpad, will clean only if needed)
